transcript.text: I'm thinking of paying my employees well
above average, but to do that I'd have
to take a pay cut myself. My thinking is
that by paying more I get more loyalty,
higher satisfaction, and most
importantly, they deliver high quality
work that keeps my customers happy. Am I
being smart or am I being naive?
>> First off, thank you for the heart
behind the question. I mean, the people
who win long-term are the people who
treat their teams well. So, thing one.
Thing two, what problem are we solving?
You can't buy loyalty. You can't buy
higher satisfaction. If you have an
attrition issue, meaning you're
employing
or number two, you have an attraction
issue, those are problems that sometimes
compensation can solve. I would say the
second one compensation solves much more
than the first. But, if you have no
churn issue and you have no attraction
issue, I would say I would keep the
extra profit and reinvest in their
skills and then once they have these new
skills and education and then create
more value in the business, that's what
I want to pay more because there's real
ROI. The idea of just giving money
because you just feel bad, I don't think
that's a a wise or prudent decision. You
want to have some return calculus for
both you and them tied to it.
